name: Chain Bridge
description: The Széchenyi Chain Bridge, opened in 1849, was the first permanent bridge across the Danube in Hungary. Designed by an English engineer and built under a Scottish one, it carries stone lions at its abutments, was blown up in 1945 and rebuilt, and ties Pest's Széchenyi Square to Buda's Adam Clark Square.

name: St. Stephen’s Basilica
description: A major Budapest church and a starting point for exploring the surrounding downtown streets.

name: Matthias Church
description: A Castle District church with a distinctive patterned roof beside Trinity Square.

name: Buda Castle District
description: Historic streets, courtyards and viewpoints above the Buda bank of the Danube.

name: Buda Castle Funicular
description: The Buda Castle Funicular, known in Hungarian as the Sikló, climbs a short, steep slope from Adam Clark Square to the castle terrace. First opened in 1870 as a steam-powered line, it was destroyed in the Second World War, rebuilt and reopened in 1986, and is run by BKV as part of city transport.

name: Hungarian Parliament
description: Hungary’s riverside parliamentary building, combining monumental architecture with official interior tours.
imageAlt: Hungarian Parliament seen from the Buda side of the Danube

name: Heroes’ Square
description: A monumental square at the Andrássy Avenue end of City Park.

name: Hungarian State Opera
description: A neo-Renaissance opera house by Miklós Ybl on Andrássy Avenue, opened in 1884. Its horseshoe auditorium, grand staircase, painted ceilings and bronze chandelier were restored in a project completed in 2022, and the company also uses the Erkel Theatre as a second venue.

name: Dohány Street Synagogue
description: A significant synagogue and Jewish heritage site in central Pest.

name: House of Music Hungary
description: A City Park building by Japanese architect Sou Fujimoto, topped by a roof perforated with 100 openings. Exhibitions on the history of music, a sound dome, a concert hall and an open-air stage are spread across three levels in the Liget Budapest museum quarter, with a separate calendar of events.

name: Margaret Island
description: A green island in the Danube between Margaret Bridge and Árpád Bridge, for walks and a break from the city streets. Motor traffic is restricted, so it is easy to explore on foot or by bike, with gardens, the Music Fountain, the Japanese Garden, the water tower, pools and a running track.

name: St. Stephen's Hall
description: A reconstructed ceremonial interior in the Buda Castle palace, designed by Alajos Hauszmann around 1900 and gutted in the Second World War. Rebuilt over decades from photographs and plans, with a large Zsolnay ceramic fireplace, it opened to visitors in 2021.

name: Museum of Fine Arts
description: Hungary's principal art museum, housed since 1906 in a neoclassical building on Heroes' Square. Its collections range from Egyptian antiquities and Greek and Roman art to Old Master paintings by Raphael, El Greco and Goya, sculpture, drawings and prints, shown alongside temporary exhibitions.

name: Andrássy Avenue
description: Andrássy Avenue is Pest's grand boulevard, laid out in the 1870s to link the inner city with City Park. Lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces and built over the Millennium Underground, it runs past the Opera House and the Oktogon to Heroes' Square and forms part of Budapest's UNESCO World Heritage listing.

name: Váci Street
description: Váci Street is the pedestrian street running south from Vörösmarty Square, long a shopping and promenading route in downtown Pest. It takes its name from the road to Vác, has a mixed German, Greek and Serbian past after 1686, and carries a mix of historic facades, souvenir shops and cafés.

name: New York Café
description: A Belle Époque coffeehouse on the ground floor of the former New York Life Insurance building on the Grand Boulevard. Its frescoed ceilings, gilded stucco and sixteen carved fauns draw visitors, and for decades writers and poets treated it as an informal office. Today it sits inside a hotel.

name: Fisherman’s Bastion
description: A terraced Castle District landmark overlooking the Danube and the Pest riverbank.

name: Shoes on the Danube Bank
description: Shoes on the Danube Bank is a memorial of sixty pairs of iron shoes along the Pest embankment, unveiled on 16 April 2005. It honours people shot into the river by Arrow Cross militiamen in 1944 and 1945, and is a place for quiet respect rather than posing for photographs.

name: Gellért Hill & Citadella
description: A dolomite hill rising above the Danube in Buda, topped by the Citadella fortress built in the 1850s and the Liberty Statue. Slopes hold a monument to Saint Gellért, a church inside a cave and wide views over the city, with the Citadella's access arrangements to check before you climb.
notice: Older tourism information includes an out-of-date renovation forecast. Confirm the current Citadella access arrangements separately before relying on an interior visit.

name: City Park (Városliget)
description: Budapest's principal city park, a rectangle about 1.4 kilometres long and just under a kilometre wide behind Heroes' Square. It staged the 1896 millennium celebrations and holds Vajdahunyad Castle, the zoo, the Széchenyi thermal bath, a lake for boating and skating, and the museums and music venue added under the Liget Budapest project.

name: Great Market Hall
description: A covered market hall for exploring food stalls and the atmosphere of a city market.

name: Margaret Island Water Tower
description: A reinforced-concrete tower in the middle of Margaret Island, completed in 1911 to supply the island with water and to serve as a lookout. Designed by engineer Szilárd Zielinski with architect Rezső Vilmos Ray, it is 57 metres high and today also hosts exhibitions and festival events.
address: Margaret Island Open-Air Stage and Water Tower

name: Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music
description: A concert hall and music academy in an Art Nouveau building by Flóris Korb and Kálmán Giergl, completed in 1907 at Liszt Ferenc Square. Zsolnay ceramics, Miksa Róth stained glass and a Liszt statue by Alajos Stróbl mark it, and a restoration won a Europa Nostra Grand Prix in 2015.

name: Pesti Vigadó
description: A Romantic-style cultural centre on the Pest embankment, designed by Frigyes Feszl and opened in 1865 on the site of an older dance hall. Liszt, Brahms and Dvořák performed there, and a restoration reopened the building in 2014 with a Danube-facing panorama terrace.

name: Vörösmarty Square
description: Vörösmarty Square is a central Pest square at the northern end of Váci Street, with a statue of the poet Mihály Vörösmarty, the Café Gerbeaud and the southern terminus of the M1 metro. It has carried many names since 1812 before taking the poet's in 1926.

name: The 1956 Monument
description: The 1956 Monument, put up in 2006 on the fiftieth anniversary of the uprising, is a government-commissioned memorial made of rusting steel columns that converge in a wedge. It stands on ground where a Stalin statue was pulled down in 1956, and it has stirred debate in Hungary ever since.

name: Gresham Palace
description: Gresham Palace is an Art Nouveau office and apartment building at the Pest end of the Chain Bridge, built in 1904-1906 for a London insurer. After decades of decline it was restored and reopened as a hotel in 2004, with Zsolnay ceramics, mosaics and peacock ironwork among its details.

name: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
description: The Hungarian Academy of Sciences, founded in 1825 after Count István Széchenyi offered a year's income from his estates, has its seat in a Neo-Renaissance palace on the Pest bank. Designed by the Berlin architect Friedrich August Stüler and inaugurated in 1865, it is decorated with statues of scholars.

name: Pál-völgyi Cave
description: A cave in the Buda hills found in 1904 and shown to visitors since 1919. Warm water rising through limestone dissolved its passages, and a guided route of about 500 metres passes dripstones, calcite crystals and sharp changes of level in a system that sources put at 12 km or more.

name: Budapest Zoo & Botanical Garden
description: Budapest Zoo and Botanical Garden in City Park opened on 9 August 1866 and is one of the oldest zoos in the world. Its main gate, Elephant House and Palm House date from the 1909-1912 reconstruction, when Art Nouveau buildings were added, and it was rebuilt after the Second World War.

name: Hospital in the Rock
description: A wartime emergency hospital built in the cave system under Castle Hill, later a secret Cold War nuclear bunker and now a museum. It treated casualties in the 1944 to 1945 siege and the 1956 uprising, and its wards and equipment can be seen on a guided tour.

name: Ludwig Museum
description: Hungary's museum of contemporary art with an international outlook grew from works donated by the collectors Peter and Irene Ludwig. It now occupies the Danube-facing wing of Müpa Budapest, where Hungarian and Eastern European art hangs alongside Western pop art, and it also runs Hungary's pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

name: Kunsthalle
description: Műcsarnok, also called the Kunsthalle, faces the Museum of Fine Arts across Heroes' Square. Built for the 1896 millennium celebrations, it follows the German Kunsthalle model: no permanent collection, just changing exhibitions of contemporary art. It is the largest exhibition space for contemporary visual art in Hungary.

name: Gellért Thermal Bath
description: A historic thermal-bath building currently closed for renovation; plan a different bath visit.
notice: Closed for renovation. The operator states that reopening is planned for 2028; this is not a confirmed booking date.

name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
description: A major thermal-bath complex in City Park with ticket types and admission rules to compare.

name: Hungarian National Gallery
description: The country's largest public collection of Hungarian fine art, displayed in the royal palace on Buda Castle hill. Founded in 1957 and installed in the castle in 1975, it holds medieval wooden altars, Gothic panel paintings and works by Munkácsy and Csontváry, and the palace also contains the Habsburg Palatinal Crypt.

name: Hungarian National Museum
description: Hungary's national museum occupies a Neoclassical building by Mihály Pollack, built between 1837 and 1847 and grown from Count Ferenc Széchényi's donation of 1802. The area in front of it is tied to the revolution of 15 March 1848, and its collections stretch from prehistory to the modern age, including the Medieval Hungarian Coronation Mantle.

name: City Park Boating Lake
description: The lake in front of Vajdahunyad Castle in City Park, where pedal boats, rowing boats and stand-up paddleboards are rented in the warmer months. In winter the same drained lakebed becomes the City Park Ice Rink, so the setting changes completely with the season.
notice: Seasonal facilities or programmes may apply. Check current operation before travelling.

name: City Park Ice Rink
description: A skating rink in City Park with a history going back to 1870, a neo-baroque main building and a surface of about 12,000 square metres. It has hosted European and world skating championships, and in warmer months the same space is flooded to form the boating lake.
notice: Seasonal facilities or programmes may apply. Check current operation before travelling.

name: The Tomb of Gül Baba
description: The Tomb of Gül Baba is an octagonal Ottoman tomb on Rózsadomb, built between 1543 and 1548 for a Bektashi dervish who died in 1541. It later served as a Jesuit chapel, was restored several times, and is described as the northernmost Islamic pilgrimage site in the world.
address: H-1023, Budapest Mecset utca 14. (entrance: Türbe tér 1.)

name: Café Gerbeaud
description: A confectionery founded in 1858 that moved to Vörösmarty Square in 1870 and took its name from the Swiss-born confectioner Emil Gerbeaud. Marble, exotic woods and Rococo-style stucco shaped the interior, and the café survived nationalisation under another name before the Gerbeaud name returned in 1984.

name: Metropolitan Ervin Szabó Library
description: The central building of Budapest's public library network is housed in the Wenckheim Palace, a neo-Baroque palace completed in 1889. Its ceremonial rooms, including a glass-roofed Imperial Staircase, the Golden and Silver Salons and two ballrooms, are preserved within a working library of more than 1.1 million volumes.

name: Museum of Ethnography
description: Hungary's museum of ethnography moved in 2022 into a new building at the edge of City Park, designed by Marcel Ferencz of NAPUR Architect. It has a planted roof garden and a facade that carries almost half a million pixels, and below ground there are nearly 7,000 square metres of exhibition space.

name: House of Terror Museum
description: A museum examining Hungary’s experiences under twentieth-century dictatorships.

name: House of Unicum
description: A visitor centre in the old Zwack distillery at Dandár utca 1, telling the story of Unicum, the Hungarian herbal liqueur. It combines period bottles, documents and family photographs with a 270-degree film, and visitors can see the old distillery and the cellar where the drink matures in oak barrels.

name: Underground Railway Museum
description: A museum inside a disused stretch of the original 1896 tunnel beneath Deák Ferenc tér. Three historic carriages from the M1 line stand on the old tracks, alongside plans, maps and models, and a Zsolnay-tiled 'Gizella tér' sign in the entrance hall recalls the line's first city-centre terminus.

name: Szamos Chocolate Museum
description: A small private museum above a Szamos café-shop on Kossuth Lajos tér, across from Parliament. Assembled by the Szamos family over about thirty years, it follows chocolate from cocoa to bar through moulds, pots, tins and marzipan sculptures. The official Szamos site lists it with guided tours booked online, but check current details before visiting.

name: Robert Capa Contemporary Photography Center
description: A photography centre at Nagymező utca 8, established in 2013, the centenary year of Robert Capa's birth and set in an Art Nouveau house of 1912. It holds a large collection of Capa prints, shows permanent displays on Capa and André Kertész, and runs temporary exhibitions, workshops and the annual Capa Grand Prize.

name: Mai Manó House
description: Built in 1894 at Nagymező utca 20 as the multi-storey studio of the court photographer Manó Mai, this neo-Renaissance house keeps its decorated facade, glass-roofed studio and Zsolnay details. Since 1999 the House of Hungarian Photography has used it for exhibitions and a photography library.

name: Vasarely Museum Budapest
description: Set in an outbuilding of Óbuda's baroque Zichy Mansion, this museum is devoted to Victor Vasarely, the Hungarian-born artist often called the grandfather of Op art. Its rooms follow him from early advertising graphics to the geometric and kinetic works of the 1960s and 1970s, with temporary shows alongside.

name: Madame Tussauds Budapest
description: Madame Tussauds Budapest fills the Palazzo Dorottya in downtown Pest, between Vörösmarty Square and the Danube promenade. It presents wax figures of Hungarian and international personalities in themed settings, including a recreated Buda Castle tunnel, and Hungarian craftspeople built many of the surrounding sets.

name: Light Art Museum (LAM)
description: The Light Art Museum, known as LAM, occupies the 1890s Hold Street Market Hall designed by Győző Czigler. It is built around light as an art form, with works by pioneers such as László Moholy-Nagy and contemporary artists. A June 2026 report announced a temporary closure, but the museum's site now lists a new exhibition, EGO, from October 2026; check it for current status.

name: Cinema Mystica Budapest
description: Cinema Mystica is an immersive audiovisual art space in the historic Párisi Udvar, at Ferenciek tere. Created by the digital artists of Global Illumination, it fills grand halls with projections, sound and interactive installations; its current show, Form in Flux, features works by 26 Hungarian and international artists.

name: IKONO Budapest
description: IKONO Budapest is an immersive, interactive art experience at Váci utca 27, in the heart of the downtown shopping street. Its rooms include a ball pit, a mirror maze and a light-painting space, created with artists such as Koketit, Heather Bellino and Kimberly Leahey, and it is part of a European IKONO network.

name: Tropicarium – The “Shark Zoo”
description: Tropicarium, known as the Shark Zoo, is a marine and tropical aquarium inside the Campona Shopping Center in Budapest's 22nd district. Opened in May 2000, it has eight halls, sand tiger and brown reef sharks seen from a 12-metre tunnel, a ray pool and a rainforest section with alligators.

name: Óbuda Museum
description: The Óbuda Museum sits in an outbuilding of the baroque Zichy Mansion on Fő tér. Its permanent exhibition, Óbuda - Three Faces of a Town, follows the district from its medieval royal days to the 1970s, with period scenes such as a manor salon, a cooper's workshop and a small inn.

name: Hungarian Jewish Museum and Archives
description: Beside the Dohány Street Synagogue, this museum and archive presents Hungarian Jewish history, ritual objects and the Holocaust. It holds Judaica and what the museum describes as Europe's most comprehensive Jewish community archives, in a 1930s building by László Vágó and Ferenc Faragó on the site of Theodor Herzl's birthplace.

name: Hungarian Museum of Trade and Tourism
description: Founded in 1966 in Buda Castle's former Fortuna Inn, this museum now stands on Korona tér in Óbuda. It follows Hungarian shops, brands, hotels and restaurants from the late 19th century to the Second World War, with recreated interiors and two rooms linked to the writer Gyula Krúdy.

name: Goldberger Textile Collection
description: On Lajos utca in Óbuda, the Goldberger Textile Collection occupies the former main building of the Goldberger company, a textile printing firm whose roots go back to the 1780s. The permanent exhibition follows the family and the factory from the 1784 blue-dyeing workshop to the winding-up of the factory, with interactive elements that explain textile printing.

name: Aquincum Museum
description: The Aquincum Museum and its archaeological park in Óbuda preserve part of the Roman civil town of Aquincum. A neoclassical museum building opened in 1894, ruins of streets, houses and a Mithras temple stand outdoors, and the best-known find is a Roman water organ dated to AD 228.

name: Budapest History Museum — Castle Museum
description: The Castle Museum occupies Building E, the southern wing of the Buda Castle palace, and tells the story of Budapest from prehistory to the late twentieth century. Its most distinctive rooms are the restored medieval palace spaces in the basement and a hall of Gothic sculpture found buried in 1974.

name: Kiscelli Museum
description: Set in a Baroque Trinitarian monastery on a plateau above Óbuda, the Kiscelli Museum shows Budapest's urban history from the eighteenth century on and houses the Budapest Municipal Gallery. Its bare-brick former church, now an exhibition and concert space, is the building's most unusual interior.

name: Budapest Gallery
description: The Budapest Gallery is the contemporary-art arm of the Budapest History Museum. Its exhibition house at Lajos utca 158 in Óbuda occupies an old dwelling house whose recorded history goes back to the early eighteenth century, and it presents Hungarian and international art across painting, photography, design and architecture.

name: Hungarian Railway History Park
description: A railway museum in a former locomotive depot in Budapest's 14th district, with a 34-stall roundhouse, a turntable and more than a hundred vehicles from steam locomotives to rare railcars. Visitors can also try a locomotive simulator and see a small railway running through the grounds.

name: Medieval Jewish Prayer House
description: A small vaulted prayer hall on the ground floor of a house in the Castle District's old Jewish quarter, with Hebrew wall paintings from the Ottoman period and tombstones in a side room off the gateway. Sources differ on how old the hall is, and it is again used for worship.

name: Petőfi Museum of Literature
description: Hungary's national literary museum fills the Károlyi Palace, a classicist building where a prime minister was arrested in 1849 and the Hungarian National Council was formed in 1918. Its collections include the manuscript of Petőfi's National Song and a complete Vizsoly Bible, and it reopened in 2023.

name: Hungarian Agricultural Museum and Library
description: Vajdahunyad Castle in City Park is a Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque ensemble designed by Ignác Alpár and built for the 1896 Millennium celebrations. The museum was founded in the same year and holds the national collection on agriculture, hunting, fishing and related food-industry material.

name: Hungarian Natural History Museum
description: Hungary's national natural history museum grew out of collections given to the National Museum in the early nineteenth century. Its exhibition building stands in the Ludovika complex in Pest's eighth district, and its collections cover anthropology, zoology, minerals and fossils.

name: Franz Liszt Memorial Museum and Research Centre
description: On the first floor of the Old Academy of Music on Vörösmarty utca, the museum preserves the apartment where Franz Liszt stayed whenever he was in Budapest from 1881 until his death in 1886. His pianos, desk, library and furniture are displayed in the rooms where he lived.

name: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
description: A museum of Asian art in the villa on Andrássy út where the optician and collector Ferenc Hopp lived. It grew from his bequest to the state and now holds Chinese, Japanese, Indian, Tibetan and other collections, with a garden that still contains the statues and pagodas he installed.

name: BudaTower – Mary Magdalene Tower
description: The Mary Magdalene Tower is the surviving part of a Gothic parish church on Kapisztrán tér in the Castle District. The church was used by Hungarians in medieval Buda, became a mosque under the Ottomans, and was demolished after the 1945 siege. The tower reopened to visitors in July 2025 under district council management, so check its current status.
notice: Budapest Info currently lists the tower as temporarily closed. Confirm admission directly before planning an interior visit.

name: Museum of Illusions
description: A compact walk-through attraction near Deák Square where visitors step into tilted rooms, a swirling Vortex Tunnel and forced-perspective set-ups. It belongs to a franchise that began in Zagreb in 2015, and 2026 reports describe a closure and renovation, so confirm its current status first.

name: Fradi Museum
description: The club museum of Ferencvárosi TC, housed in the club's stadium in Budapest's ninth district. Exhibits include a reconstructed dressing room and wooden stand, shirts, trophies and Flórián Albert's Ballon d'Or, and a visit can be paired with a tour of the arena itself.

name: Lukács Thermal Bath
description: A thermal bath in Buda's Felhévíz district whose springs have been used for centuries. Wikipedia traces bathing on the site to at least the 12th century, and the present complex developed from the 1880s onward. Over time it became a favourite of Hungarian writers, composers and filmmakers, and it still has a medical side.

name: Rudas Thermal Bath
description: A Buda bath beside Erzsébet Bridge whose Ottoman core, an octagonal pool under a dome on eight columns, dates from the 16th century. Later wings add a swimming pool and a modern wellness area. Its gender-separated apron bathing was added to Hungary's national intangible heritage list in October 2026.

name: Palatinus Bath
description: Budapest's first outdoor beach on Margaret Island, opened in 1919 and expanded in the 1930s with a modernist changing building and a wave pool. Its thermal-well water, historic mosaics and year-round indoor wellness section, added in a 2017 reconstruction, make it one of the city's most layered bathing complexes.
notice: Seasonal facilities or programmes may apply. Check current operation before travelling.

name: Veli Bej Bath
description: A small Ottoman bath of the 1570s, set inside the grounds of a hospital in Buda's 2nd district. A central dome sits over an octagonal pool, the Hospitaller order restored it in the early 2010s, and archaeological finds from the work are on display. It is among the few Ottoman baths in Budapest still in use.

name: Aquaworld Resort Budapest
description: A large indoor water park and hotel complex in northern Budapest that opened in December 2008 under a Ramada name. A glass dome 73 metres wide covers the leisure area, which has eleven slides, a wave pool and a surf pool. Check its current name and operator before travelling.

name: Lupa Beach
description: A sandy beach resort on Lupa Lake, a former quarry in Budakalász, just north of the Budapest city limits. It was developed by Sziget Festival founder Károly Gerendai, who opened it in 2016. The lakeside setting includes watersports and play areas and is seasonal.
notice: Seasonal facilities or programmes may apply. Check current operation before travelling.

name: Római Open-Air Bath
description: A summer-season open-air bath in Óbuda's Rómaifürdő district, on ground that once belonged to Roman Aquincum. The present layout dates from 1964 and was modernised around 2000, with a swimming pool, an adventure pool and several slides. The nearby Danube riverbank is a separate, newer public beach.
notice: Seasonal facilities or programmes may apply. Check current operation before travelling.

name: Millenáris Park
description: A park of nearly six hectares in Buda's 2nd district, built around the former Ganz electrical works. Preserved factory halls now serve as event spaces and the National Dance Theatre, while the newer Széllkapu Park adds walkways, solar-topped pavilions and a suspended garden that, according to the official site, looks towards Margit körút and the Castle District.

name: Kopaszi-gát
description: A long Danube embankment in south Buda, created as a regulation dam between 1870 and 1876 to reduce ice floods. After decades of industry and landfill it was redeveloped from 2006 as a landscaped park with cafés, a playground and views across Lágymányos Bay towards the BudaPart quarter.

name: Zugliget Chairlift
description: Hungary's first passenger ropeway, opened on 20 August 1970, carrying double chairs for 1,040 metres from Zugliget up János Hill, a rise of 262 metres. Its nickname Libegő, meaning floater, won a public naming contest, and the top station is a short walk from the Erzsébet lookout.

name: Children’s Railway
description: A 760 mm narrow-gauge line of about 11 km through the Buda hills between Széchenyi-hegy and Hűvösvölgy, opened in stages from 1948 to 1950. Children aged roughly 10 to 14 perform most station and train duties under adult supervision, a practice recognised by Guinness World Records in 2015.

name: Normafa
description: A meadow and plateau in the Buda hills, named after a beech tree struck by lightning in 1927, with a view over the city. It has been used for walking and winter sport for well over a century, and a phased renovation since the mid-2010s has added paths, a playground and visitor facilities.

name: Bartók Béla Boulevard
description: A long Buda road climbing gently from the Gellért area through Móricz Zsigmond körtér towards the Feneketlen-tó lake, now lined with cafés, galleries and bookshops. It has carried several names since the 1870s and has been called Bartók Béla út since 1945.

name: National Dance Theatre
description: Hungary's National Dance Theatre now stands in Millenáris Park in Buda, in a converted former factory that opened in February 2019. Before that it was based in the former Carmelite monastery and church in Buda Castle, a building that had been a theatre since the 1780s.

name: Müpa Budapest
description: A riverside arts complex in Ferencváros combining the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall, the Festival Theatre and the Ludwig Museum under one roof. It opened in 2005 as the Palace of Arts and was renamed Müpa in 2015; its main hall is known for adjustable acoustics and a large organ.

name: Budapest Music Center
description: A concert hall, jazz club, music library and record label in a converted 1890 building at Mátyás utca 8. The organisation was founded in 1996 by trombonist László Gőz and moved into its own premises in 2013, presenting classical, contemporary and jazz music.

name: Castle Garden Bazaar
description: A neo-Renaissance complex of arcades, stairways and gardens by Miklós Ybl at the foot of Castle Hill, beside the Danube. Built in the 1870s and 1880s, it later served as a rock-concert venue, then as a ruin, before its restoration and reopening in 2014.

name: Clark Ádám Square and the 0 km Stone
description: The roundabout at the Buda end of the Chain Bridge, named after the engineer Adam Clark and home to the limestone 0 km stone from which Hungary's main roads are numbered. The Buda Castle Funicular and the tunnel under Castle Hill start here.

name: Hungarian Heritage House
description: A national institute for Hungarian folk culture based in the former Budai Vigadó on Corvin Square, built in 1898-1900. It runs folk dance houses, craft courses, concerts, exhibitions and archival work, and it is also the base of the Hungarian State Folk Ensemble.

name: Vienna Gate
description: A rebuilt gateway at the northern end of the Castle District, where several well-known streets meet. The present gate dates from 1936, marking 250 years since the recapture of Buda, and replaced older gates that stood here since the Middle Ages.

name: The Tabán
description: A green slope between Buda Castle, Gellért Hill and Naphegy, on the site of the old Tabán quarter of winding streets, taverns and Serbian, Greek and German residents. The district was largely demolished in the 1930s, and today a quiet park near Döbrentei Square marks its place.

name: Matthias Fountain
description: A neo-Baroque bronze fountain group by Alajos Stróbl in the Buda Castle palace forecourt, showing King Matthias Corvinus on a hunt. It was inaugurated in 1904, damaged in the Second World War, and is sometimes nicknamed the Trevi Fountain of Budapest.

name: Savoyai Terrace
description: A broad terrace in front of the Hungarian National Gallery on the Danube side of Buda Castle, with views of the Parliament, Gellért Hill and the bridges. Its centrepiece is József Róna's equestrian statue of Prince Eugene of Savoy, installed in 1900.

name: Tóth Árpád Promenade
description: A tree-lined walk along the castle wall in Buda Castle District, laid out on the line of an old defensive passage. It looks out toward the Buda hills, Tabán and Gellért Hill, carries the name of the poet Árpád Tóth, and is known for the Japanese ornamental cherries that bloom along it in spring.

name: Garden of Philosophers
description: A small sculpture garden on the side of Gellért Hill, where eight life-size bronze figures by Nándor Wagner face a shared centre. Religious founders and thinkers stand together in a work meant to show what cultures have in common. It was a gift from the sculptor's widow and was unveiled in 2001.

name: Cave Church
description: A church built into natural and artificial caves on the side of Gellért Hill, linked to the Pauline order. Founded after Hungarian pilgrims visited Lourdes in the 1920s, it was walled up under communism and reopened as that era ended; thermal water keeps the interior mild.

name: Trinity Square
description: The main square of the Castle District, where Matthias Church, the Fisherman's Bastion and the Baroque Holy Trinity Column meet. The column was inaugurated in 1713 after a plague epidemic, and the square took its open shape only after the Ottoman rule ended in 1686.

name: St Elizabeth Church — Rózsák tere
description: The Roman Catholic parish church of St Elizabeth of Hungary stands on Rózsák tere in Erzsébetváros. Designed by Imre Steindl, the architect of the Hungarian Parliament, it has two 76-metre neo-Gothic towers, a richly furnished interior and a statue of the saint in front, from which the Square of Roses takes its name.

name: St Anne's Church — Batthyány Square
description: St Anne's is the Baroque parish church of Felsővízváros, the upper part of Buda's Víziváros, on Batthyány tér across the Danube from the Parliament. Begun in 1740 and completed in 1761 according to most sources, it is entered by steps down from the square, and the parish is known for its Jehmlich organ.

name: Inner City Parish Church of the Assumption
description: The Inner City Parish Church of the Assumption sits at the Pest end of Elisabeth Bridge, which was designed as an arch so the church could stay. A Gothic hall church that served as a mosque under Ottoman rule, it still has a mihrab, and Roman fort remains were found beneath it in 2014 to 2016.

name: Deák Square Lutheran Church
description: A plain neoclassical Lutheran church at Deák Ferenc tér 4, designed by Mihály Pollack and built between 1799 and 1808, with a Doric-pilastered façade rebuilt by József Hild in 1856. It is an active Lutheran parish church and stands next to the Evangelical National Museum.
sourceLabel: Hungarian Wikipedia — Deák téri evangélikus templom

name: Saint Emeric Cistercian Church
description: The Buda Cistercian Saint Emeric Church at Villányi út 25 is a neo-Baroque parish church consecrated in 1938 and designed by Gyula Wälder. Its twin towers face Feneketlen Lake in Szentimreváros, and it stands beside the Cistercian school; the parish has again been run by the order since 1989.

name: Saint Margaret Parish Church — Lehel Square
description: The Árpád-házi Szent Margit-templom, popularly the Lehel tér church, is a neo-Romanesque parish church in Újlipótváros designed by István Möller and modelled on the Zsámbék church ruin. Built from 1931 to 1933, it has frescoes by Henrik Heintz and stained glass by Miksa Róth.

name: Saint Ladislaus Church — Kőbánya
description: Ödön Lechner's Kőbánya church mixes Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, Persian and Hungarian folk motifs. Built from 1894 to 1899 and consecrated in 1900, it has Zsolnay tiles and altars, and among Budapest churches only St Stephen's Basilica is taller than its 83-metre tower.

name: Óbuda Synagogue
description: The Óbuda Synagogue at Lajos utca 163 is a neoclassical synagogue consecrated in 1821 and designed by András Landherr. After decades as a warehouse and television studio it was rededicated in 2010 and is again an active Orthodox prayer house maintained by EMIH, a Chabad-linked community.

name: Serbian Orthodox Church — Downtown Pest
description: The Church of Saint George on Szerb utca is the Serbian Orthodox parish church of central Pest and, according to Wikipedia, the only Serbian Orthodox church in the capital today. Its Baroque building dates from 1733, its tower from 1752, and its garden wall holds old Serbian gravestones.
sourceLabel: Wikipedia — Church of Saint George, Budapest

name: Queen of Heavens Church — Újpest
description: The Queen of Heavens Church, or Egek Királynéja-templom, is the main Roman Catholic parish church of Újpest. Built between 1875 and 1881 to plans by József Kauser in a neo-Gothic style, it stands on Szent István tér, the main square of a town founded only in 1840.
sourceLabel: We Love Budapest — Szent István tér, Újpest

name: Holy Family Church — Terézváros
description: The neo-Gothic Holy Family Church at Szondi utca 67 was built in 1930 and 1931 for a fast-growing Terézváros. Heavily damaged on New Year's Day 1945, it was rebuilt and reconsecrated in 1948, and its high altar was later clad in marble paid for by the composer Zoltán Kodály.
sourceLabel: Budapest City Library (FSZEK) — Holy Family Church

name: Armenian Catholic Church — Újbuda
description: The Armenian Catholic church at Orlay utca 6 in Szentimreváros serves Budapest's Hungarian-Armenian Catholic community and is dedicated to Our Lady of Ransom and Saint Gregory the Illuminator. It grew out of a villa bought in the 1960s, and the parish centre was renovated with state support in 2022.
sourceLabel: Budapest City Archives — Armenian community study (2024)

name: Pozsonyi Road Reformed Church
description: The Pozsonyi úti Reformed Church, known as the Hálaadás or Thanksgiving church, stands at Pozsonyi út 58 in Újlipótváros. Built between 1936 and 1940 to designs by Imre Tóth and Jenő Halászy, it has a classical portico, a separate tower and Bauhaus-influenced interiors, and its basement once sheltered people in hiding.
sourceLabel: Pozsonyi Road Reformed Parish — Church of Thanksgiving

name: Rumbach Street Synagogue
description: Rumbach Street Synagogue, designed by Otto Wagner and consecrated in 1872, is an octagonal Moorish Revival synagogue in the Jewish Quarter of Erzsébetváros. After decades of decay it was restored and reopened in 2021, and, according to its official site, it is still a synagogue that also hosts concerts and events and serves as an exhibition space of the Jewish Museum and Archives.
sourceLabel: Center for Jewish Art — building history

name: Kazinczy Street Orthodox Synagogue
description: The Kazinczy Street Synagogue is the great Orthodox synagogue of Pest's Jewish Quarter, built in 1912 and 1913 by the Löffler brothers in an Art Nouveau style influenced by Ödön Lechner. A Hebrew inscription crosses its brick facade, and the complex around it has included a school and a ritual bath.

name: Újlak Synagogue — Frankel Leó Street
description: The Frankel Leó Street Synagogue, known earlier as the Újlak Synagogue, is a neo-Gothic brick synagogue consecrated in 1888 and later enclosed by a 1920s residential building. It is the home of an active Neolog congregation in Buda's 2nd district, and it appeared in the 1999 film The Taste of Sunshine.
